title: Differential criterion for an etale coordinate map
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $U$ a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-over-base, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] smooth over $k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], $u\in U$ and $d\geq0$. Let $h_1,\ldots,h_d\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$, and let $h:U\to\mathbf A^d_k$ be the $k$-morphism whose coordinate functions are these $h_j$ [def-sbc-affine-space]. Use the differential sheaf $\Omega_{U/k}$ [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf] and the residue field $\kappa(u)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. If the classes $dh_1,\ldots,dh_d$ form a $\kappa(u)$-basis of $\Omega_{U/k,u}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{U,u}}\kappa(u)$, then there is an open neighbourhood $U'\subseteq U$ of $u$ such that $h|_{U'}:U'\to\mathbf A^d_k$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Here a basis means a linearly independent spanning family, and the tensor is module base change [def-weil-module-base-change].

source.place: Tag 02GU (lemma-etale-at-point), square-Jacobian criterion (8), applied on a standard smooth chart from Tag 01V7 (lemma-smooth-locally-standard-smooth); Tag 00T7 (algebra.tex, lemma-standard-smooth) supplies the differential basis of that chart. The chosen-coordinate consequence: on a standard smooth chart k[y_1,...,y_N]/(F_1,...,F_r) with N-r=d, adjoin the relations H_j-T_j over k[T_1,...,T_d] for lifts H_j of the h_j; the differential-basis hypothesis makes the square N-by-N Jacobian invertible at u, which is condition (8) of Tag 02GU.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-coordinate-differentials-affine-chart] to choose an affine open W containing x and a submersive presentation P with r+d variables, r relations, and P.map the first-r inclusion. Retain its canonical cotangent-fibre isomorphism Phi and its equality identifying the prescribed coordinate morphism with Spec of polynomial evaluation followed by the affine-space spectrum isomorphism. Pull the given fibre basis back along Phi; its specified values make it the family 1 tensor d(h_j restricted to W).

By [lem-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-kahler-basis], the complementary last-d variables give a global basis of Omega_{A/k}, where A=Gamma(W,O). Reindex this basis and the prescribed fibre basis by ULift(Fin d). Apply [lem-pur-etale-coordinates-of-fibre-basis] to the evaluation A to kappa(x). This gives f in A with nonzero evaluation at x and an etale polynomial evaluation map k[T_j] to A[1/f] sending T_j to h_j restricted to W, then localized.

Let l:Spec A[1/f] to Spec A be the localization map and i=l followed by the affine-chart immersion into U. The polynomial universal property [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] identifies the localized coordinate map with l followed by the original evaluation map. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine] and the chart equality show that i followed by the prescribed coordinate map is etale. By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion], i is an open immersion with image V=D_W(f). Evaluation of f at x is nonzero, so x is in V. The canonical isomorphism from Spec A[1/f] to V carries i to V.ι, and etaleness is invariant under that isomorphism. This proves the claimed restriction etale.

lean.statement: theorem Scheme.exists_etale_open_of_coordinate_differentials_basis (k : Type u) [Field k] (U : Scheme.{u}) [U.Over (Spec (.of k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (U ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (U ↘ Spec (.of k))] [Smooth (U ↘ Spec (.of k))] (x : U) (d : ℕ) (h : Fin d → Γ(U, ⊤)) (hbasis : ∃ b : Module.Basis (Fin d) (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (U.presheaf.stalk x)) (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (U.presheaf.stalk x) ⊗[U.presheaf.stalk x] ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor U.toRingedSpace x).obj (U ↘ Spec (.of k)).relativeDifferentials)), ∀ j : Fin d, b j = TensorProduct.tmul (U.presheaf.stalk x) (N := (RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor U.toRingedSpace x).obj (U ↘ Spec (.of k)).relativeDifferentials) (1 : IsLocalRing.ResidueField (U.presheaf.stalk x)) ((U ↘ Spec (.of k)).relativeDifferentials.presheaf.germ ⊤ x trivial ((U ↘ Spec (.of k)).relativeDifferentialsDerivation.d (h j)))) : ∃ V : U.Opens, x ∈ V ∧ Etale (V.ι ≫ AffineSpace.homOfVector (U ↘ Spec (.of k)) (fun j : ULift.{u} (Fin d) ↦ h j.down))
